subject: VertexWave x Redwood — batching tiers beta + next steps
body:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sarah Kim <sarah@vertexwave.ai>, Daniel Ortiz <daniel@vertexwave.ai>
Date: Sat, Feb 15, 2025 at 9:12 AM PST
Subject: VertexWave x Redwood — batching tiers beta + next steps
Attachments: VertexWave_Redwood_BatchingTiers_BenchmarkSummary_v0.3.pdf

Sarah, Daniel —

Thanks again for the deep dive yesterday. Per your cost + tail-latency goals, I wanted to send:

1) Beta opt-in instructions for the workload-aware batching tiers
2) A short benchmark summary (attached)
3) A proposed time for a follow-up next week

---
Beta opt-in (Hosted API)

You can opt in per request (recommended for POC) by setting:

- batching_tier: "cost_efficient" (or "standard" / "fast")

Example (JSON body fragment):
{
  "model": "llama-3.1-70b-instruct",
  "messages": [...],
  "batching_tier": "cost_efficient"
}

Notes:
- This is safe-by-default: if the service is overloaded we’ll fall back to a compatible profile rather than letting queue delay grow unbounded.
- If you already set explicit batching knobs in your config (max_batch_size, max_queue_delay_ms, etc.), those overrides will take precedence over the tier.

What we recommend for VertexWave (based on what you shared):
- Chat streaming routes: start with "standard" (then trial "fast" if you need token cadence) 
- Non-streaming summarization / batch jobs: trial "cost_efficient"

Supported for this beta cohort (your account is whitelisted):
- Regions: us-east-1, us-west-2
- Models: llama-3.1-70b-instruct, qwen2.5-72b-instruct (plus a couple of smaller variants on request)

---
Validating it’s working

In the attached benchmark summary, you’ll see p95 latency and $/1M tokens deltas across the three tiers. For your POC, the simplest validation is:
- Compare p95 end-to-end latency for the same prompt set under standard vs cost_efficient
- Track timeout/cancel rates (should not increase)

If you send me the route mix (streaming vs non-streaming) and your current timeouts, I can suggest a quick measurement plan.

---
Next check-in

Can you do either of these?
- Tue 2/18 11:00–11:30am PT
- Thu 2/20 1:00–1:30pm PT

If neither works, send 2–3 windows and I’ll adjust.

Best,
Aditya

—
Aditya Rao
Product, Redwood Optimize
Redwood Inference


From: Daniel Ortiz <daniel@vertexwave.ai>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, Feb 15, 2025 at 12:47 PM PST
Subject: Re: VertexWave x Redwood — batching tiers beta + next steps

Thanks Aditya — super helpful.

Two questions before we flip anything:

1) Can we enable per route (we have a streaming chat endpoint and a separate non-streaming “analysis” job)?
2) Is there a way to confirm the “effective” tier or batching config being applied (header/response metadata)?

Also, we’re currently pinned to us-west-2. Prefer to keep the first test there.

2/20 1pm PT works on our side.

-Daniel


From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwoodinference.com>
To: Daniel Ortiz <daniel@vertexwave.ai>, Sarah Kim <sarah@vertexwave.ai>
Date: Sat, Feb 15, 2025 at 1:10 PM PST
Subject: Re: VertexWave x Redwood — batching tiers beta + next steps

Daniel —

1) Yes, per route is the intended pattern.
   - You can set batching_tier per request, so your streaming chat stays on standard while the non-streaming job tries cost_efficient.
   - If you later move to a config-level default, we can do that per deployment / per route as well.

2) Confirming “effective” config:
   - Today: easiest is via latency + queue delay metrics (I can share the exact fields we watch; also happy to jump on a quick screenshare).
   - Coming shortly: we’re rolling out an “effective config/explain” surface that returns the computed tier + any overrides. It’s not broadly GA yet; I can ask Eng to enable it for your POC if you need it for auditability.

And yes — us-west-2 is fine for first tests.

I’ll send a calendar invite for Thu 2/20 1:00–1:30pm PT.

Best,
Aditya


From: Sarah Kim <sarah@vertexwave.ai>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sun, Feb 16, 2025 at 9:22 AM PST
Subject: Re: VertexWave x Redwood — batching tiers beta + next steps

Aditya —

Invite received, thanks.

One note: our primary UX risk is streaming cadence. We can tolerate a bit higher p95, but if we start seeing long gaps between tokens, it’s a problem (we have a ~200–250ms “feels snappy” guideline).

If you have any specific guidance on which tier is safest for streaming, send it over.

-Sarah


From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sarah Kim <sarah@vertexwave.ai>, Daniel Ortiz <daniel@vertexwave.ai>
Date: Sun, Feb 16, 2025 at 10:08 AM PST
Subject: Re: VertexWave x Redwood — batching tiers beta + next steps

Sarah —

Makes sense. For streaming, the safest starting point is:
- Tier: standard
- Keep your current timeouts unchanged for the first pass

We generally recommend avoiding cost_efficient on streaming until you’ve confirmed token cadence is stable for your prompt distribution and concurrency (cost_efficient can trade queue time for throughput under load).

On Thursday, if you can share:
- typical prompt length (rough buckets are fine)
- concurrent streaming sessions at peak
- your current timeout settings

…we’ll propose a “standard for streaming + cost_efficient for batch” split and a minimal dashboard checklist to validate both p95 and token cadence.

See you then.

Best,
Aditya
